sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Recall that the graph of an even function must be symmetric about the [MATH: y]-axis.

  • Graphs II, III, and IV are not symmetric about the [MATH: y]-axis. So, they are not even functions.

  • On the other hand, graph I is symmetric about the [MATH: y]-axis. That is to say, if we reflect graph I over the [MATH: y]-axis, we get the same picture. This means that graph I is an even function.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

items.readable_text:
Content:
Recall that the graph of the even function [MATH: f(x) = x^2] is symmetric about the [MATH: y]-axis.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/75d3bad6abdd7c8bef29ae917d8fe095]

Content:
Notice the following:

Content:
[MATH: f(− 1)|= 1 = f(1); f(− 2)|= 4 = f(2); f(− 3)|= 9 = f(3); =⋮]

Content:
So, for every [MATH: x] in the domain, both [MATH: x] and [MATH: -x] give the same value of the function. Algebraically, this fact can be written as follows: [MATH: f(-x) = f(x).]

Content:
In general, a function [MATH: f(x)] is said to be even if
[MATH: f(-x) = f(x)]
for each [MATH: x] in the domain of the function.

Now, recall that the graph of the odd function [MATH: g(x)=x] has rotational symmetry of order [MATH: 2] about the origin.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/e458b0ef70f7e56313bc191d92672759]

Content:
Notice the following:

Content:
[MATH: f(− 1)|= − 1 = − f(1); f(− 2)|= − 2 = − f(2); f(− 3)|= − 3 = − f(3); =⋮]

Content:
So, for every [MATH: x] in the domain, [MATH: x] and [MATH: -x] give opposite values of the function. Algebraically, this fact can be written as [MATH: f(-x) = -f(x).]

Content:
In general, a function [MATH: f(x)] is said to be odd if
[MATH: f(-x) = -f(x)]
for each [MATH: x] in the domain of the function.

items.title: Classifying Even and Odd Functions Using the Algebraic Definition

sections.normalized_html: Is the function [MATH: f(x)=|x| -1] even, odd, both, or neither?
sections.readable_text: Is the function [MATH: f(x)=|x| -1] even, odd, both, or neither?

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Remember that

  • a function is even if [MATH: f(-x) = f(x)] for all [MATH: x,] while

  • a function is odd if [MATH: f(-x) = -f(x)] for all [MATH: x.]

Computing [MATH: f(-x)] for the given function and comparing it to [MATH: f(x),] we have [MATH: f(− x)|=|(− x)|− 1; =|x|− 1; = f(x).] Since [MATH: f(-x) = f(x),] the function is even.

Lastly, we compute [MATH: -f(x)] and get [MATH: − f(x)|= − (|x|− 1); = −|x|+ 1.] Since [MATH: f(-x) \neq -f(x),] the function is not odd.

Therefore, the function is only even.

sections.readable_text:
The table below defines the function [MATH: g(x).] Given that [MATH: g(x)] is an even function, find the value of [MATH: a+b.]

| [MATH: x] | [MATH: -5] | [MATH: -4] | [MATH: -1] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 4] | [MATH: 5] |
| [MATH: g(x)] | [MATH: 20] | [MATH: 11] | [MATH: -4] | [MATH: a-3] | [MATH: 11] | [MATH: b+5] |

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Since [MATH: g(x)] is an even function, we must have that [MATH: g(-x)=g(x).]

Using the fact that [MATH: g(-1) = g(1),] we obtain

[MATH: g(− 1)|= g(1); − 4|= a − 3; a|= − 1.]

Using the fact that [MATH: g(-5) = g(5),] we obtain

[MATH: g(− 5)|= g(5); 20|= b + 5; b|= 15.]

Finally, [MATH: a+b = -1 + 15 = 14.]

Item 9 — Tutorial: The Algebraic Definition of Even Functions

Content:
Recall that the graph of the even function [MATH: f(x) = x^2] is symmetric about the [MATH: y]-axis.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/75d3bad6abdd7c8bef29ae917d8fe095]

Content:
Notice the following:

Content:
[MATH: f(− 1)|= 1 = f(1); f(− 2)|= 4 = f(2); f(− 3)|= 9 = f(3); =⋮]

Content:
So, for every [MATH: x] in the domain, both [MATH: x] and [MATH: -x] give the same value of the function. Algebraically, this fact can be written as follows: [MATH: f(-x) = f(x).]

Content:
In general, a function [MATH: f(x)] is said to be even if
[MATH: f(-x) = f(x)]
for each [MATH: x] in the domain of the function.

Item 11 — Example: Classifying Even and Odd Functions Using the Algebraic Definition

Example Prompt:
Is the function [MATH: f(x)=|x| -1] even, odd, both, or neither?

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Remember that

- a function is even if [MATH: f(-x) = f(x)] for all [MATH: x,] while
- a function is odd if [MATH: f(-x) = -f(x)] for all [MATH: x.]

Computing [MATH: f(-x)] for the given function and comparing it to [MATH: f(x),] we have
[MATH: f(− x)|=|(− x)|− 1; =|x|− 1; = f(x).]
Since [MATH: f(-x) = f(x),] the function is even.

Lastly, we compute [MATH: -f(x)] and get
[MATH: − f(x)|= − (|x|− 1); = −|x|+ 1.]
Since [MATH: f(-x) \neq -f(x),] the function is not odd.

Therefore, the function is only even.

Using the fact that [MATH: g(-1) = g(1),] we obtain

Using the fact that [MATH: g(-5) = g(5),] we obtain
